title: The Clip in the Group Chat
banner: Your ending came from your written answers, not from which option you picked.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.about: Your closest friend. Works hard, and is shy on camera

lisa.name: Lisa
lisa.about: The funny one. Films and posts almost everything

marco.name: Marco
marco.about: Plays football for the university team

dev.name: Dev
dev.about: Quiet. Usually goes along with the group

scenes.title: The Bus
scenes.description: The last bus home, at night. Sarah looks out of the window with her earphones in, and you sit just behind her. Across the aisle, Lisa shows Marco a video on her phone, and Dev stands in the aisle holding the pole.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's Tuesday night, and you're on the last bus home with Lisa, Marco, Dev and Sarah.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah is your closest friend. She works hard, she's a bit shy, and she gave her first big presentation today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa is the funny one. She films and posts almost everything, and she doesn't always stop to think first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Marco plays football for the university team, and he can talk about it for hours.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dev is quiet. He's usually on his phone, and he tends to go along with whatever the group does.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The presentation was hard for Sarah. She froze for a few seconds, and she's still a bit shaken.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now she's looking out of the window with her earphones in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the aisle, Lisa is watching something on her phone. She filmed Sarah's moment from the audience.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She shows it to Marco and Dev, and they laugh quietly so Sarah doesn't hear.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You notice, but you don't say anything, and neither does anyone else.

scenes.title: Ping
scenes.description: A dark dorm room at night. You sit on the bed, seen from behind. Your phone lights your hands. A lamp glows on the desk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Later that night, you're in your room when your phone buzzes.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: Haha, I can't stop watching this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's a clip of Sarah freezing in her presentation, and Lisa has added a joke caption.

lines.speaker: marco
lines.text: Haha, this is so good.

lines.speaker: dev
lines.text: Send this to the housemates' chat too.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: 12 people are in this chat. Sarah isn't one of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everyone in the chat is laughing, but you don't think it's funny.

scenes.title: Your Move
scenes.description: Close on your phone. Chat bubbles float in the dark, like paper cut-outs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody asked Sarah before sharing it, and she has no idea the clip exists.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: This is so funny, right?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa is your friend. She doesn't mean any harm. She just finds it funny and takes it lightly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But you know how badly Sarah took today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You have two choices.

scenes.title: Two More Groups
scenes.description: Three phones in a row, joined by paper strips like a paper chain. Each one shows the clip.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By midnight, the clip has already been forwarded to other chats.

lines.speaker: dev
lines.text: Just sent it to the housemates' chat.

lines.speaker: marco
lines.text: Sent it to my football group too. They love it.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: Now it's in three chats, and anyone in them can save it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa still hasn't deleted it, and she hasn't written back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa hasn't replied. Everyone else is still laughing in the chat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah has gone to bed, and she has no idea about any of this.

scenes.title: Morning
scenes.description: The campus café, Wednesday morning. You stand behind Sarah in the queue. Marco and Dev are near the counter, looking at their phones.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's Wednesday, 8:30 am, at the campus café.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Overnight, someone put the clip on the public campus page, and it already has hundreds of views.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: People in the café look at their phones, then at Sarah.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Morning. Why is everyone looking at me?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah's phone ran out of battery overnight, so she hasn't seen a single message.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She has no idea about the clip, but you do. Marco and Dev are standing nearby.

scenes.title: Sarah Knows
scenes.description: A café table. Sarah sits across from you, and you are seen from behind. The light is softer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You take Sarah to a table by the window, away from everyone.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Thank you for telling me first. It helps, a little.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You tell Sarah about the clip now, about ten minutes later than you should have.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I know you tried to stop it, and I get that. I just wish you'd told me first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah's hands are shaking a little.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I don't want a fight. I just want it gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah picks up her bag and leaves. She doesn't even take her coffee.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa walks in laughing. She sees the look on your face and stops.

scenes.title: Lisa's Excuse
scenes.description: A corner of the café by the door. Lisa faces you. You are seen from behind. The light is flat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You tell Lisa that Sarah has seen the clip and walked out upset.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: What? It was just one joke.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: I only shared it with close friends.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: And I didn't put it on the campus page. That wasn't me.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: I didn't think anyone would forward it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa sounds a bit sorry, but mostly she just wants this conversation to end.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: Come on. You know me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's Friday, two days later. You check the chats and the campus page again.

options.label: Message Lisa privately.
options.sub: Ask her to take it down, just between you two.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Can you delete the clip? Sarah never said it was okay.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: It's a joke! She'll never see it.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Lisa doesn't delete the clip, and she doesn't say she will.

options.label: Reply in the group chat.
options.sub: Say it where everyone can see.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Can we take this down? Sarah never agreed to it.

beat.speaker: marco
beat.text: Relax. It's just a joke.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: Wow. Okay.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Marco tells you to relax, and Lisa sounds annoyed. Nobody else says anything, and Lisa stops replying.

options.label: Tell Sarah what is happening.
options.sub: Take her aside and tell her now.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Sarah, can we sit down? Someone posted a clip of your presentation.

beat.speaker: sarah
beat.text: A clip? Which clip?

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: You show her the clip, and she looks shocked. Strangers are already commenting on it.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Marco and Dev still have the clip on their phones.

options.label: Report the post and ask Marco and Dev to delete it.
options.sub: Get the clip taken down before you talk to Sarah.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Marco, Dev, please delete that clip right now. I'm reporting the post too.

beat.speaker: marco
beat.text: Fine. Deleted.

beat.speaker: dev
beat.text: Other people already saved it, though.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Two copies are gone, but the post is still up, and plenty of people saved the clip. Sarah is still waiting for her coffee and has no idea.

d3.prompt: What do you say to Lisa?

options.label: Accept her excuse.
options.sub: Say you know she didn't mean any harm.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Okay. I know you didn't mean for this to happen.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: Thank you. I'll tell them to stop.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Lisa relaxes, and things between you two feel fine. But Sarah still hasn't heard anything from her.

options.label: Hold her responsible.
options.sub: Say the clip was her choice.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: You filmed it and shared it, and you didn't ask Sarah first. That part is on you.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: That's not fair!

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: ...I didn't think.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Lisa looks embarrassed and a bit hurt. She stops arguing.

why1.question: The clip is now in three chats. Who is responsible for what? Think about Lisa, Marco and Dev, Sarah, and you. Write 2 to 4 sentences.
why1.helper: 2 to 4 sentences. There's no right answer, but reasons help.

followups.why1_fu_consequence: You've said who did what. Can you add what could happen to Sarah because of it?
followups.why1_fu_parties: You've named one person. Who else played a part, and what did they do?
followups.why1_fu_split: Can you split it up? What's Lisa's part, and what's the part of the people who forwarded it?

why1.harder: Now try it from Sarah's side. She isn't in the chat and never agreed to the clip. What does she need from each person, and who can actually give it?
why1.nudge: Can you say a bit more? Two or three sentences about who did what would be great.
why1.ackHarder: Thanks. That brings in a side the chat never heard.

why2.question: Lisa says she only shared the clip with close friends and didn't expect anyone to forward it. Do you agree with her? Give your reasons. Write 2 to 4 sentences.
why2.helper: 2 to 4 sentences. There's no right answer, but reasons help.

followups.why2_fu_reason: You've said what you think. Can you say why? Give one reason for your view.
followups.why2_fu_consequence: Think about Sarah. What changes for her if Lisa's excuse is accepted, and what changes if it isn't? Add one of those to your answer.

why2.harder: What's the best reason someone could give for the opposite view? Does it change your mind?
why2.nudge: Can you say a bit more? Do you agree with Lisa, and why?
why2.ackHarder: Thanks. It helps to hear the other side.

A.title: A Way Forward
A.description: Warm, low sun on the library steps. Sarah, Lisa and you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Over the last two days, you talked with Lisa, Marco and Dev about what happened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah asks to meet on the library steps. Lisa, Marco and Dev are there too.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: I filmed you without asking, and I shared it, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Thank you. I want it gone from every chat and from the campus page.

lines.speaker: marco
lines.text: We shouldn't have passed it on. I'm sorry, Sarah. It's deleted.

lines.speaker: dev
lines.text: Same. Sorry. I'll tell the others to delete it too.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: Lisa writes in all three chats: "I filmed Sarah without asking. Please delete the clip and don't share it."

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: The replies come in: "Deleted." "Sorry, Sarah." "Done."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Within an hour, the clip is gone from all three chats, and the campus page takes it down after you all report it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A few people might still have a copy, but nobody is laughing anymore.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: From now on, ask before you film or post anyone. That's all I wanted.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: Deal. Never again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah finally smiles. You all head to class together.

ask.question: What do you think Sarah needed most from Lisa, Marco and Dev?

explain: Lisa said what she did and said sorry without Sarah having to ask, and Marco and Dev did the same. That's what made it possible to talk.
The clip came down in all three chats and on the campus page. Some copies might still exist, so there's still some risk for Sarah, and that can't be undone.
In your answers, you separated who did what: filming, forwarding and responding. That helped you act without taking Sarah's choices away from her.

B.title: Still Out There
B.description: Flat grey-blue light on the library steps. A bench with nothing on it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah doesn't come to tutorial, and her seat is empty.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: The clip is still in two chats and on the campus page, and new comments keep coming.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa avoids you. Marco and Dev say it's old news.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody has said sorry to Sarah, so she's dealing with this on her own.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You open a message to Sarah, but you haven't written anything yet.

ask.question: The clip is still in two chats and on the campus page. What do you think would help most now?
taps: Everyone deletes it and reports the post

explain: In this story, nobody took full responsibility. Lisa never said sorry, the people who forwarded the clip stayed quiet, and Sarah was left to deal with it alone.
Your answers named some of the people involved, but they didn't always say who owed what or what it meant for Sarah. That makes it hard to know where to start.
It's not too late in the story. A clear sorry, asking people to delete the clip and reporting the post, and asking Sarah what she wants would all still help.
B.explainIfSkipped: You chose not to write some of your answers, so this ending comes from the story alone. Nobody in it said who owed what, and Sarah was left to deal with it on her own.

choiceLines.d1_private: You messaged Lisa privately, so she wasn't embarrassed in front of everyone. But that also gave the clip more time to spread.
choiceLines.d1_group: You replied in the group chat, and everyone saw you speak up. But Lisa may have felt called out.
choiceLines.d2_tell: You told Sarah first, so she heard it from someone who cares. But she was still upset in a public place.
choiceLines.d2_delete: You reported the post and asked for the clip to be deleted first, and some copies were removed. Sarah heard about it later and wished she'd been told first.
choiceLines.d3_accept: You accepted Lisa's excuse, so the friendship stayed calm. But Lisa didn't have to face what she did.
choiceLines.d3_hold: You held Lisa responsible, so she had to face it. The friendship felt shaky for a while.

closing: There's no single right path. Someone else might choose differently and still have good reasons. What matters here is being able to say who's responsible for what, and why.

items.title: Posted
items.text: Lisa filmed Sarah's worst moment and shared it in a chat of 12.

items.title: Forwarded
items.text: Marco and Dev sent it on to two more chats.

items.title: Went public
items.text: Someone put it on the campus page, and strangers started commenting.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Let's look back. Lisa filmed Sarah during her presentation and shared it, and it reached three chats and a public page before Sarah even knew.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: It can happen to anyone, and it happens fast. A joke gets forwarded, and nobody stops to think how it feels for the person in the clip.

slides.title: Who should have seen it coming?

people.name: Lisa
people.should: Ask Sarah first, or don't share it. She had the first chance to stop it.

people.name: Marco and Dev
people.should: Say no. Every forward puts it in front of more people.

people.name: Everyone in the chat
people.should: One person saying "delete this" could have changed it.

people.name: You
people.should: Speak up early, and tell Sarah before she hears it from strangers.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Some people should have seen this coming much sooner.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Lisa filmed Sarah and shared the clip, so she was the first person who could have stopped it.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Marco and Dev forwarded it, and every forward put it in front of more people.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: And the people who laughed along and said nothing made it feel okay.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: You were the one who noticed. Speaking up early, and telling Sarah yourself, was the strongest move anyone had.

items.title: Ask first
items.text: Would Sarah be okay with this? If you don't know, ask her, or don't share it.

items.title: Don't pass it on
items.text: Every forward is a new choice. You can stop it with one tap.

items.title: Speak up and report
items.text: Say it's not okay and ask for it to be deleted. Report it if it's public, and tell Sarah yourself.

items.title: Make it right
items.text: Delete it, say sorry and mean it, and ask Sarah what she needs.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Here is how it could have gone. First, ask before you film or share anyone.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Second, don't pass it on. Every forward is a new choice, and you can stop it with one tap.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Third, speak up. Say it's not okay, report it if it's public, and tell Sarah yourself before she hears it from someone else.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: And if it has already gone wrong, make it right. Delete it, say sorry, and ask Sarah what she needs.

slides.title: The moral
slides.moral: Ask before you share. If it goes wrong, own it and make it right.
slides.note: A joke is only a joke if the person in it agrees.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Remember this. A joke is only a joke if the person in it agrees.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Ask before you share. And if it goes wrong, own it and make it right.

reflect.offer: Want to try one more? It's a short, similar situation.
reflect.scenario: A friend sends you a screenshot of a private chat. In it, a classmate says something personal. Your friend says: "Send it to the class group, just for a laugh."
reflect.question: What do you think happens next if you pass it on? Write one or two sentences about who is affected and how.
reflect.ref_harder: What's one thing you could do at the start to change how it turns out?
reflect.ref_ack: Thanks. That's the end of the story.
